source.citation: Glover, Jones, Kempton and Oveson, Effects of backtracking on PageRank, Applied Mathematics and Computation 531 (2026) Article 130182

boundary: 'proved' means a written proof in the manuscript (some steps are exact identities checked by the code), not formal verification; 'certified' means an exhaustive or finite exact rational computation, claimed only for the stated finite cases (census: five damping values, orders 2-7); 'numerical' means floating-point evidence only; 'open' is not claimed. Internal AI-assisted review is not peer review or independent reproduction.

claims.statement: House graph, uniform restart, eps=1/2: pi_0(4)=638/3615, pi_1(4)=22/125, pi_inf(4)=8/45; both endpoints lie strictly above the middle value, so the roof coordinate is not monotone in mu and the coordinatewise clause of Conjecture 3.1 (hence the conjecture) fails.
Closed cubic-over-cubic formula for the roof score pi_mu(4) as a function of s=(1-eps)mu with coefficients polynomial in eps.

The roof coordinate is monotone in mu on [0,inf) iff eps <= eps_c ~ 0.2406813 (unique root in (0,1/4)); otherwise it has exactly one strict minimum, located at mu=1 iff eps=4/9; failure occurs already for mu in [0,1].
For the roof, pi_0 and pi_inf lie on the same strict side of pi_1 (so the endpoint shortcut gives the wrong direction) iff eps > eps_0 ~ 0.3291038.
The gem with uniform restart has a nonmonotone coordinate for every eps < eps_g ~ 0.3565988.

Among connected simple graphs of minimum degree >= 2 with uniform restart, order five is the smallest order with a nonmonotone coordinate, for every fixed eps in (0,1) (house for eps > eps_c, gem for eps < eps_g).
claims.computationalCheck: census orders <= 5 consistent; proof in prose

claims.statement: With leaves allowed (forced return at leaves, statements for mu > 0), P3, K2 and K3 are mu-invariant; the paw is nonmonotone iff eps in (0,eps_1) U (eps_2,1), eps_1 ~ 0.0783255, eps_2 ~ 0.4355202; every other four-vertex graph is monotone. Hence the smallest order with leaves allowed is 4 for eps < eps_1 or eps > eps_2 and 5 for eps_1 <= eps <= eps_2.
claims.computationalCheck: results/verification.json: symbolic (all six order-four responses, exact Sturm counts)

claims.statement: The five-vertex tree with edges 04,13,23,34, uniform restart, eps=1/2: leaf 1 has pi_mu(1)=(21mu^2+95mu+84)/(15(9mu^2+42mu+37)), strictly decreasing to a minimum at mu=(2 sqrt 22 - 7)/9 ~ 0.2645 and then increasing; exact certificate pi_{1/10}=9371/61935, pi_{1/4}=349/2307, pi_{1/2}=547/3615. Trees are not always monotone.
Backtracking PageRank lifts through finite graph covers; hence for every k >= 2 there are connected graphs of order 5k with a fixed positive fraction of nonmonotone vertices.
claims.computationalCheck: legacy_checks: independent_exact_cover_solves (6); lemma is an instance of PageRank invariance under fibrations (Boldi et al.)

claims.statement: Small-damping criterion (uniform restart, minimum degree >= 2): if the two-step profile f_k(mu) has an interior strict extremum with margin delta > 0 at three points a<b<c, then pi_mu(k) is nonmonotone for every 0 < eps < delta/(n+delta); if all sigma_j = d_j/d_k - h_j (j ~ k) have the same weak sign, f_k is monotone and any nonmonotonicity is of order eps^3 or higher.

claims.statement: Exact formula for d pi_mu(i)/d mu at mu=1 and three one-sided endpoint tests, each sufficient for nonmonotonicity.
claims.computationalCheck: checked exactly at 3985 census vertices; at eps=1/2 the tests detect 285 of 478 nonmonotone vertices with no false positives

claims.statement: Exact census of all 995 connected graphs on 2-7 vertices at eps in {1/10,1/4,1/3,1/2,17/20}, on mu in [0,inf) and (0,1), using exact Sturm root counts on open intervals; e.g. 353 of 507 seven-vertex graphs of minimum degree 2, and 675 of all 853 seven-vertex connected graphs, have a nonmonotone coordinate for some listed eps. Order-7 counts on (0,1) at the five eps: 50/68/75/85/44 (min degree 2) and 113/141/156/172/89 (all connected). Certified only at the five listed damping values.
claims.computationalCheck: results/census_full.json; results/verification.json: census, root_counter_regressions (synthetic responses, Atlas 399, 256 known-root cases); agrees with an independent Sturm implementation of the post-revision audit on all 33,900 coordinates

claims.statement: The spread clause fails as printed (diamond for every eps, by formula; house at eps=1/2 by eight exact values) and when reversed (six-vertex graph with edges 01,04,05,12,23,34,35 at eps=17/20). The house part and the reversed reading are finite exact certificates; the diamond part is proved for every eps. Even with unique extreme vertices for every mu (seven-vertex graph with edges 03,04,12,13,14,25,26,34,56 at eps=17/20) the spread increases from mu=0 to mu=1/10, so uniqueness of the extrema does not rescue the reversed clause.

For connected graphs of minimum degree >= 2 and restart v, the full vertex score vector is independent of mu iff P^2 v = v; equality of the full vectors pi_1 and pi_inf at one damping value is already equivalent. Sufficiency for regular and biregular graphs is from Glover et al. and Arrigo et al.; the converse is new within the search.

On standard and random networks (2-cores, uniform restart), 10-41% of vertices are nonmonotone, excursions are small, the endpoint shortcut is wrong for up to 26% of vertices and rankings are stable (Kendall tau >= 0.93).

Les Miserables 2-core (n=59, m=236), eps=1/2: Fauchelevent and Pontmercy are ordered the same way at mu=0 and mu=inf but oppositely at mu=1. A finite exact-arithmetic search of the 507 seven-vertex min-degree-2 graphs at eps in {1/2,17/20} and seven mu grid points found no such pair (grid points only; not a certificate between them).
With minimum degree >= 2, n pi_inf(i) <= (1+eps d_i/2)/(1+eps), so the score tail is never heavier than the degree tail.

For every tail index alpha > 1, clique chains of minimum degree two have regularly varying limiting degree law with index alpha while n pi_inf stays below 4/3, so Conjecture 3.2 fails in its local-weak-convergence reading. Mechanism adapted from Henning, van der Hofstad and Litvak.

claims.statement: In a configuration model with i.i.d. positive degrees, n pi_inf(U) should converge in law to a variable Z whose tail transfer from the degree is elementary; the graph-level convergence (model, conditioning, degree hypotheses, local convergence of the radius-two functional) is not proved and is stated as an open problem.
